title: Dangerously Yours
paragraphs: A dramatic anthology led by Victor Jory, presenting romantic adventure, historical drama, espionage, and literary stories in which love and danger are closely intertwined.
CBS romantic/adventure anthology starring Victor Jory. Historical corpus comprises two auditions plus sixteen numbered regular broadcasts.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Pre-series auditions (June 20, 1944 to June 21, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and CBS/Vicks regular run (July 2, 1944 to October 15, 1944) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Victor Jory (performer), Jean Holloway (writer and radio adaptor), Mark Warnow (music director and music), Richard Sanville (director), Gertrude Warner (performer), [[person|jackson-beck|Jackson Beck]] (performer), and Alfred Noyes (author).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to romantic adventure and doomed love, World War II-era commercial network radio, historical adventure, literary adaptation, heroic outlaw and swashbuckling figures, and Dangerously Yours to Matinee Theater production lineage.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Dangerously Yours 1944 CBS/Vicks run, Partial surviving Dangerously Yours corpus, Transition from Dangerously Yours to Matinee Theater, and Commercial network drama during World War II.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|matinee-theater|Matinee Theater]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|cloak-and-dagger|Cloak and Dagger]].
